Phyllodes tumor of the breast: The histological features of bland spindle cell proliferation with negative cytokeratin stains and the presence of a well-circumscribed mass with a characteristic whorled pattern are consistent with a phyllodes tumor of the breast. The patient's history of breast cancer and the location of the new lesion in the inferolateral aspect of the right breast also support this diagnosis.
Metaplastic spindle cell carcinoma: The negative cytokeratin stains and the presence of a spindle cell proliferation could also be consistent with a metaplastic spindle cell carcinoma. However, the bland appearance of the cells and the lack of other characteristic features of metaplastic carcinoma, such as squamous or mesenchymal differentiation, make this diagnosis less likely.
